private.name: Humanoid

data.narrative:
Orchard Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $25.8M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Humanoid, and Walden Robotics), supplemented by one public comparable and a broader universe of eight private frontier-tech peers in robotics and manufacturing.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised ($26M) as a proxy base and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next financing stage, yields $52M. Peer-median analysis across the five same-sector comparables produced a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, seed stage) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The wide range reflects stage variance within the comp set; Series B peers cluster at $1.6B–$2.0B, while Series A peer Humanoid is valued at $1.4B.

These methods triangulate to a range of $44M (floor, stage-progression) to $1.9B (ceiling, upper-quartile peer). The median implied valuation is $851M. Key uncertainties include revenue/unit economics at Orchard, the applicability of later-stage comps to a Series A company, and execution risk inherent in early-stage robotics ventures. Stage-progression and peer-median methods diverge materially, suggesting valuation will depend heavily on company-specific metrics and investor conviction on technology differentiation.
